verdict: Supermicro's sales more than doubled to $10.2B from a year ago and gross margin recovered to 9.9%, lifting profit to $483M — though working capital swallowed $6.6B of cash in the quarter.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: vs 6.3% in Q2 FY26 and 9.6% a year ago

kpis.label: Cash flow from operations
kpis.note: used in Q3; capex and investments were $97M

segments.name: Total net sales
segments.note: Supermicro reports a single operating segment and printed no product split this quarter. Sales are mostly complete AI server and rack systems built on its Data Center Building Block Solutions.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing next-generation servers, racks and Data Center Building Block Solutions; up 32% YoY.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing; up 49% YoY.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Back office, legal and facilities; up 24% YoY.

otherDetail: Non-operating items were a net $14.9M expense: $4.1M of other income, plus $45.4M of interest income, less $64.5M of interest expense. A separate $0.7M share of loss from an equity investee, net of taxes, is shown as equityM (amounts from thousands).
oneTimers: The May 5 release called its figures preliminary; the Form 10-Q filed May 11, 2026 reported the same quarter totals (net sales $10,243M, net income $483M).
Stock-based compensation was $125.9M in the quarter — the main gap between GAAP net income ($483M) and non-GAAP net income ($581M basic).
footerNote: Supermicro guided Q4 FY26 net sales to $11.0B–$12.5B.

takeaways.title: Sales more than doubled
takeaways.text: Net sales rose to $10.2B from $4.6B a year ago, driven by AI rack demand — though sales eased from $12.7B in Q2 as large deals timed differently.

takeaways.title: Margins recovered
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose to 9.9% from 6.3% in Q2, which management credited to its growing Data Center Building Block Solutions business.

takeaways.title: Cash went the other way
takeaways.text: Operations used $6.6B of cash in the quarter as receivables and inventories ballooned with the sales surge; cash ended at $1.3B against $8.8B of bank debt and convertible notes.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Mar 31, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)

follow100Note: Supermicro kept $4.72 of every $100 — margin recovered from Q2, but at 9.9% gross margin most of each sales dollar still goes straight to building the systems.
